invariants.invariant: At most one AuthIdentity exists per (provider, providerSubject) among non-deleted rows — a Google/Facebook identity resolves to exactly one Account.
invariants.enforcement: Partial unique index UQ_identity_auth_identities_provider_subject (pre-existing migration 1786791535416-CreateIdentityAccessSchema) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND provider_subject IS NOT NULL; TypeOrmAuthIdentityRepository.translateUniqueViolation now also maps this constraint's violation to DomainError.conflict('provider_identity_already_exists', ...) (previously only the LOCAL provider_identifier constraint was translated).

cases.operation: Two concurrent OAuth callbacks for the same brand-new providerSubject race to insert the AuthIdentity (replayed/double-submitted callback)
cases.expected: The loser's insert fails on UQ_identity_auth_identities_provider_subject, is translated to a conflict, and OAuthLoginUseCase re-resolves the winner's identity and issues a session for it instead of surfacing a user-facing error or leaving a half-created Account
cases.test: libs/modules/identity-access/test/oauth-login.use-case.spec.ts > self-heals a double-submitted/replayed callback: a provider_subject unique-violation on create resolves to the winner's session instead of failing (unit); apps/api/test/oauth-flow.e2e-spec.ts > handles two truly concurrent first-time callbacks for the same brand-new provider identity as a real Postgres race: exactly one account graph, no raw 500s (fix-request-review-3 #6 — real Promise.all race with a synchronization barrier inside the mocked exchangeCodeForProfile, replacing a previous sequential completeCallback()/completeCallback() pair that never actually exercised the unique-constraint conflict path); the pre-existing sequential 'logs into the same account on a second, later callback' test is retained separately to cover ordinary repeat-login, not race recovery

cases.expected: QueryFailedError with constraint=UQ_identity_auth_identities_provider_subject is translated to DomainError.conflict('provider_identity_already_exists', ...); the pre-existing provider_identifier -> phone_already_exists mapping is unaffected

invariants.invariant: The optional `address` supplied at self-registration is written to the same UserProfile row created in the account-creation transaction, or left null when omitted — never a separate/partial write.
invariants.enforcement: RegisterUseCase forwards address into CreateAccountUseCase.execute (unchanged transaction boundary — CreateAccountUseCase already wrote address for admin-created accounts; this closes the gap for public self-registration), which passes it to USER_PROFILE_PROVISIONER.provision inside the same UnitOfWork.withTransaction as the Account/AuthIdentity/AccountRole writes.

cases.expected: 201, and GET /user-profiles/:id returns the same address string
cases.test: apps/api/test/auth-flow.e2e-spec.ts > stores the optional address supplied at registration on the provisioned UserProfile

cases.expected: 201, and GET /user-profiles/:id returns address: null (no default/placeholder value)
cases.test: apps/api/test/auth-flow.e2e-spec.ts > registers successfully when the optional address is omitted

cases.operation: RegisterUseCase.execute passes its address field straight through to CreateAccountUseCase.execute's input
cases.expected: createAccount.execute is called with address preserved verbatim
cases.test: libs/modules/identity-access/test/register.use-case.spec.ts > creates the Account via CreateAccountUseCase and issues a PUBLIC-portal session, like a successful login

invariants.invariant: Self-registration commits or rolls back the entire Account/AuthIdentity/AccountRole/UserProfile/RefreshSession graph as one operation — a session-stage failure (permission check, token issuance, refresh-session persistence) never leaves a committed account behind (fix-request-review-3 #3, AC6 'trong 1 giao dịch nhất quán').
invariants.enforcement: RegisterUseCase.execute wraps its entire flow (CreateAccountUseCase.execute call + permission check + token issuance + RefreshSession.save) in a single owning unitOfWork.withTransaction; TypeOrmUnitOfWork.withTransaction was made reentrant (joins the already-active TypeOrmQueryRunnerContext instead of opening a second, independent connection/transaction), so CreateAccountUseCase's own withTransaction call participates in the same outer transaction rather than committing on its own.

cases.operation: Refresh-session issuance (tokenService.issueAccessToken/issueRefreshToken) fails after the Account/AuthIdentity/AccountRole/UserProfile writes have already happened in the same (still open) transaction
cases.expected: 500, and the entire transaction rolls back — no Account, AuthIdentity, AccountRole, UserProfile or RefreshSession row is committed; the same phone is free to register again immediately afterward
cases.test: apps/api/test/auth-flow.e2e-spec.ts > register (changes/cycle-002 addendum) > atomicity: refresh-session issuance failing after account/profile/role writes > leaves no Account/AuthIdentity/AccountRole/UserProfile committed, and the phone is free to register again (e2e, real Postgres, TOKEN_SERVICE forced to reject in an isolated NestJS testing module)

cases.operation: A use case's own withTransaction call is invoked while already inside another use case's active transaction (the general reentrancy mechanism this invariant depends on)
cases.expected: No second QueryRunner/connection is created; the nested call runs inside the outer transaction and does not commit or roll back independently of it
cases.test: libs/platform/database/test/typeorm-unit-of-work.spec.ts > joins an already-active transaction instead of opening a second connection, and lets the outer call own commit/rollback; > rolls back the single outer transaction when a nested withTransaction call throws

invariants.invariant: First-time OAuth account provisioning commits or rolls back the entire Account/AuthIdentity/AccountRole/UserProfile/RefreshSession graph as one operation — a session-stage failure after the account graph is written never leaves a committed social account with no session behind (fix-request-review-006 #2).
invariants.enforcement: OAuthLoginUseCase.provisionAndIssueSession wraps createAccountForProfile + issueSessionForAccount (token issuance + RefreshSession.save) in a single owning unitOfWork.withTransaction, reusing the same reentrant TypeOrmUnitOfWork mechanism as RegisterUseCase. On a provider-subject unique-constraint conflict (concurrent-callback race), that transaction has already rolled back in full (TypeOrmUnitOfWork.withTransaction calls rollbackTransaction() before rethrowing) by the time the catch block re-resolves the winner and calls issueSessionForAccount again — which then opens its own fresh, separate transaction since no ambient one exists.

cases.operation: Refresh-token issuance fails after the Account/AuthIdentity/AccountRole/UserProfile writes have already happened in the same (still open) transaction, for a brand-new OAuth identity
cases.expected: The callback redirects with oauth=error&reason=oauth_failed and no refresh cookie; the entire transaction rolls back — no Account, AuthIdentity, AccountRole, UserProfile or RefreshSession row is committed; a retry with a fresh callback provisions cleanly
cases.test: apps/api/test/oauth-flow.e2e-spec.ts > rolls back the entire first-time account graph when session issuance fails after the graph is written (fix-request-review-006 #2) (e2e, real Postgres, TOKEN_SERVICE.issueRefreshToken forced to reject once via jest.spyOn)

cases.operation: Two truly concurrent first-time callbacks for the same brand-new provider identity race on the provider-subject unique index (retained from the pre-existing invariant, re-verified against the refactored transaction boundary)
cases.expected: Exactly one account graph is committed; the loser's failed transaction leaves no partial state, and both callbacks converge on the winner's session
cases.test: apps/api/test/oauth-flow.e2e-spec.ts > handles two truly concurrent first-time callbacks for the same brand-new provider identity as a real Postgres race: exactly one account graph, no raw 500s (unchanged by this cycle's refactor, re-run and re-verified)
